deals.whyRanked: Cheapest verified fare of the five at $108–145 RT nonstop, and the Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area is 25 minutes from downtown.
deals.soloWhy: The BeltLine trail and Old Fourth Ward are dense and walkable, though you'll want rideshare between the farther-flung neighborhoods.

highlights: Atlanta BeltLine walk through Old Fourth Ward and Ponce City Market
Martin Luther King Jr. National Historical Park
Jimmy Carter Presidential Library and Museum
Chattahoochee River NRA — Cochran Shoals or Sope Creek trails
Krog Street Market for lunch
itinerary: Day 1 — Old Fourth Ward walking tour, MLK Jr. NHP, BeltLine stroll to Ponce City Market for dinner.
Day 2 — Chattahoochee River NRA (Cochran Shoals loop, easy 3-mile trail), afternoon at the Jimmy Carter Library.
Day 3 — Krog Street Market and Cabbagetown murals, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: MARTA rail covers downtown, Midtown, and the airport well; a rental car or rideshare is worth it for the Chattahoochee day.
guide.stayArea: Old Fourth Ward or Midtown — both walkable to the BeltLine and close to MARTA.

deals.travelWindow: Sep 7 – Oct 17, new nonstop route just launched this year
deals.whyRanked: JetBlue's brand-new BOS–VPS nonstop is running $135–205 RT introductory fares, and Gulf Islands National Seashore is about 20 minutes away.
deals.soloWhy: The Destin Harbor boardwalk is walkable for an evening, but the beaches and shopping are spread out along Route 98 and mostly need a car.

highlights: Destin Harbor Boardwalk at sunset
Gulf Islands National Seashore's Okaloosa Day Use Area beach
Crab Island sandbar (boat tour or rental)
HarborWalk Village shops and fishing charters
Henderson Beach State Park's dune trail
itinerary: Day 1 — Destin Harbor Boardwalk, HarborWalk Village, sunset dinner on the water.
Day 2 — Gulf Islands National Seashore's Okaloosa unit for a beach day, or a Crab Island boat trip.
Day 3 — Henderson Beach State Park dune trail and a final beach morning, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: A rental car is close to essential — the beaches and shopping stretch for miles along Route 98 with no transit.
guide.stayArea: Near the Harbor or Miramar Beach — both put you close to restaurants and a short drive from the National Seashore.

deals.whyRanked: $144–180 RT nonstop, and Everglades National Park's Shark Valley entrance is under an hour from downtown.
deals.soloWhy: South Beach and Wynwood are dense, walkable, and full of solo diners at sidewalk cafes, with the free Metromover covering downtown.

highlights: Ocean Drive and South Beach's Art Deco Historic District
Wynwood Walls street art
Little Havana's Calle Ocho and Máximo Gómez Park
Shark Valley's 15-mile loop trail (bike or tram) in the Everglades
Vizcaya Museum and Gardens
itinerary: Day 1 — Art Deco walking tour of South Beach, Ocean Drive at sunset.
Day 2 — Wynwood Walls in the morning, Little Havana for a late lunch and dominoes at Máximo Gómez Park.
Day 3 — Rent a car, Shark Valley tram or bike loop in the Everglades, back for a swim before the flight home.
guide.gettingAround: The free Metromover covers downtown and Brickell; South Beach is walkable on its own. Rent a car only for the Everglades day.
guide.stayArea: South Beach or Brickell — both walkable with easy rideshare access to everything else.

deals.whyRanked: $152–236 RT nonstop across two carriers, and Red Rock Canyon is a 20-minute drive from the Strip.

nearbyParks.name: Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area

deals.soloWhy: The Strip and Fremont Street are made for wandering solo and striking up conversation, though it's a scene-driven trip more than a quiet one.

highlights: Fremont Street Experience at night
Red Rock Canyon's 13-mile scenic drive and Calico Tanks trail
The Strip on foot — Bellagio fountains to the Venetian
Valley of Fire State Park's red-sandstone formations
Downtown's Neon Museum
itinerary: Day 1 — Walk the Strip from Bellagio to the Venetian, fountain show at sunset, dinner off-Strip.
Day 2 — Rent a car, Red Rock Canyon scenic drive and the Calico Tanks hike (2.5 mi round trip).
Day 3 — Fremont Street and the Neon Museum, or push out to Valley of Fire, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: The Strip and Fremont Street are walkable on their own; rent a car only for the Red Rock or Valley of Fire day trips.
guide.stayArea: The Strip for convenience and nightlife, or Downtown/Fremont for a cheaper, more local base.

deals.travelWindow: Sep 6 – Oct, cheapest per JetBlue one-way sale fares
deals.whyRanked: $223–270 RT nonstop to one of the most walkable solo-friendly islands in the country, with El Yunque National Forest 40 minutes away.
deals.soloWhy: Old San Juan is compact, colorful, and safe to wander alone end to end, with rideshare covering the rest of the metro.

highlights: Castillo San Felipe del Morro and Castillo San Cristóbal
Old San Juan's colorful streets and the Puerto Rican flag door on Calle Imperial
El Yunque's La Mina Falls trail
Condado Beach for a swim
Piñones food kiosks along the coast
itinerary: Day 1 — Old San Juan walking tour, both Spanish forts, dinner in the old city.
Day 2 — Rent a car, El Yunque National Forest for the La Mina Falls trail (easy, ~0.7 mi each way), Piñones kiosks on the way back.
Day 3 — Condado Beach morning, Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: Old San Juan and Condado are walkable; rideshare covers the rest of the metro, and a rental car is worth it for the El Yunque day.
guide.stayArea: Old San Juan (historic, walkable) or Condado (beachfront, more nightlife).
